title: Counting to Ten on the Lisbon Coast: Williams Wins by Twelve
title_candidates: Counting to Ten on the Lisbon Coast: Williams Wins by Twelve
Seven Double Figures, One Comfortable Winner
The Atlantic Ledger: Williams 149, Everyone Else Their Own Worst Enemy
Williams Takes a Third Trophy While the Field Practises Its Tens
theme: Portugal handed out double figures to almost everyone — seven scores of 10 or worse across four days — and the Trophy went to the man who kept posting the best round in the field in between his own; Williams's 38-41-41 was simply more than the carnage could eat into.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck; affectionate ribbing of insiders, never zany
opening_hook: Open on the ledger of double figures — Meller's 10 at the 3rd on day one, Neumann's 11 at the 10th, Williams's own two 10s — then reveal that the man with two of them won by twelve; the tens are the connective tissue, Williams's three field-best rounds are the answer.
foreshadow: Stuart Neumann arrives having finished 3rd on the Trophy in each of the last three TEGs, and has never held a Wooden Spoon
Alex Baker arrives as the reigning Wooden Spoon holder, last of six in TEG 7
David Mullin arrives on back-to-back Jacket wins; Gregg Williams has been 5th on gross in each of the last three TEGs
Henry Meller's 10 at the 3rd in R1 is the tournament's first double figure — and nothing like the last

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams (winner, 149 pts, by 12 from Alex Baker)
competitions.how: Williams took the outright lead at R1 H10 and was never headed across the remaining 62 holes. He built it rather than inherited it: best round in the field three times (38, 41, 41), outscoring Baker in three of four rounds. The lead went 4, 11, 5, 12 — the only wobble was a below-median 29 at Quinta da Marinha in R3, complete with a 10 at the 11th, which cost six of the eleven-point cushion and nothing else. Baker's own arithmetic damns him: even playing his personal average in his worst round he still loses by eight.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +77, by 6 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Mullin took outright gross command at R1 H13 and held it for 36 holes, three rounds' worth of front-running, before Jon Baker prised it away at R3 H13 (b17) after Mullin's worst round to date. Baker led by two overnight; Mullin reclaimed the lead outright at the 2nd hole of R4 at Oitavos Dunes and immediately went clear, closing with a field-best 17 — eight better than Baker on the day — for a sixth Jacket and a third in succession. Best gross round in the field in three of four rounds.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.winner_or_loser: Stuart Neumann (loser, 100 pts, 11 behind Henry Meller)
competitions.how: Neumann was bottom outright from R1 H4 and stayed there for all 68 remaining holes — bottom of the field in every single round, below the field median in all four. R1 was the ruin: 17 points, +43 gross, 29 shots bled across holes 7-15, both personal worsts. R3 at Quinta da Marinha compounded it — 10 at the 1st, 9 at the 4th, 8 at the 9th, 11 at the 10th, 20 points. His R2 (31) and R4 (32) were the better halves of a 15-point spread, and the attribution is 'inherited': Meller actually outscored him in two of four rounds and still finished ahead of him, because Meller's own R4 implosion arrived too late to matter.

Wednesday on the Estoril Coast: One Man Scores, One Man Counts

Penha Longa, Mountain Parkland, Flat Refusal to Blink
rounds.chosen_headline: Sintra Bows: Williams's 41 Buys an Eleven-Point Cushion
rounds.angle: The hardest layout of the four yields the tournament's decisive round — Williams goes eleven holes without dropping a net shot, survives a 10 at the 12th, and stretches the lead from four to eleven while Mullin's +14 gross opens a six-shot Jacket gap.

rounds.chosen_headline: Return to Quinta da Marinha: The Field Rediscovers Double Figures
rounds.angle: The only repeat venue turns into the carnage round — Neumann's 10 at the 1st and 11 at the 10th, Alex Baker's 10 at the 8th, Williams's 10 at the 11th, Mullin's worst round to date — and it still only trims the Trophy lead to five, while Jon Baker takes the Jacket lead after Mullin's 36 holes in front.

headline_candidates: Oitavos Dunes: Meller Loses 22 Shots in Six Holes, Williams Loses Nothing in Ten
The Links Finale: One Man Clean Home, One Man Counting to Ten at the 4th
Mullin Reclaims the Jacket at the 2nd; Williams Signs for 41 and a Third Trophy
rounds.chosen_headline: Oitavos Dunes: Meller Loses 22 Shots in Six Holes, Williams Loses Nothing in Ten
rounds.angle: The Atlantic links closes the ledger — the defending Trophy champion posts 10 and 9 inside the first five holes, Mullin retakes the gross lead at the 2nd and never gives it back, and Williams plays the last ten without dropping a net shot for 41 and a twelve-point win.

players.arc: Two prior Trophies become three: three best-in-field rounds (38, 41, 41), a 10 in each of two of them, and a twelve-point win that never looked like being interrupted — while extending his run of finishing 5th on gross to a fourth straight TEG, which bothers him not at all.

Front-runs the gross for 36 holes, hands it to Jon Baker at R3 H13 after his worst round to date, then takes it straight back at the 2nd hole of R4 and closes with a field-best 17 for a sixth Jacket and a third in a row.
The reigning Wooden Spoon holder turns up, makes a 10 at the 8th, a 9 at the 17th and a 9 at the last across the week, and still finishes second on the Trophy — improvement measured in tens.
Two rounds of quiet accumulation put him in front of his brother's playing partners and briefly in the Green Jacket lead, before Mullin's R4 removes six shots and the argument in a single afternoon.
Third on the Trophy in each of the last three TEGs, bottom of the field in all four rounds of this one: 17 points and +43 in R1, a 10 and an 11 in R3, and a first Wooden Spoon by eleven.

The defending champion's title defence ends on the beach at Oitavos — 22 shots gone in six holes, a 10 at the 4th and a 9 at the 5th — and he finishes second-bottom, saved from the Spoon only by Neumann's head start.

venue_notes: TEG's 2nd visit to the Lisbon Coast, and a rare three-course itinerary in which nobody had seen anything before. Play up the family joke: R1 at Quinta da Marinha (Robert Trent Jones Sr., pine forest and ocean views) then R2 at Penha Longa (Robert Trent Jones Jr., mountain parkland in the Sintra hills) — father on Wednesday, son on Thursday, both unsympathetic. R3 returns to Quinta da Marinha, the only repeat venue of the tournament and the one that produced the most damage second time round. R4 at Oitavos Dunes, Portugal's premier links and a Portuguese Open host, provides the Atlantic finale where Meller's tournament expires and Williams's is confirmed.
course_history_notes: Every course was new to every player — no prior TEG history exists on the Lisbon Coast beyond the area's 2nd visit.
Quinta da Marinha was the only course played twice: gross returns there ranged from Jon Baker's 89 in R3 to Neumann's 114 in R1.
Penha Longa, on paper the hardest layout, produced the two best gross rounds of the tournament: Mullin's 86 and Jon Baker's 91.
Oitavos Dunes yielded Mullin's 88 and Williams's 93 on the closing day, and Meller's 111.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R2 at Penha Longa — Williams's field-best 41 turned a four-point lead into eleven; the R3 29 clawed it back only to five, and it was never threatened again.
Green Jacket: R4 H2 at Oitavos Dunes — Mullin's outright retake of the gross lead from Jon Baker, 34 holes after losing it, and the start of an eight-shot round-four swing.
Wooden Spoon: R1 H4 at Quinta da Marinha — Neumann drops to the bottom outright and stays there for all 68 remaining holes.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up as the prominent frame: seven double figures from five players is genuinely the tournament's connective tissue, and it flatters rather than obscures Williams, who made two of them and still won by twelve.

why_the_champion_won: Williams built it: best round in the field three times (38, 41, 41), outscoring Alex Baker in three of four rounds, so that a below-median 29 in R3 — 10 at the 11th and all — cost him six points of an eleven-point cushion and nothing more; Baker playing his own average in his worst round still loses by eight.
storyline_note: Framed as a catalogue of the field's double figures rather than a straight Trophy chronicle, because the tens are what everyone will remember — but Williams stays the spine of it: he owns two of the seven and won by twelve anyway, and the 'why' is stated in the Trophy section and the opening.
